newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua seeks to block mass deportation from US.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua seeks to block mass deportation from US.

text.p: Nicaraguan Foreign Minister Emilio Alvarez, fearing mass deportations of some 40,000 Nicaraguans from the United States, on Wednesday said he would urge U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to delay the process.
"We want this to be much slower than what they think is a good pace because right now Nicaragua cannot receive this quantity of people," Alvarez told a news conference.
He said he would ask Albright during a meeting with other Central American foreign ministers in Washington on April 2 to delay the expulsions.

He said a recent change in U.S. immigration law meant that Nicaraguans with less than seven years residence in the United States who have received deportation orders can no longer appeal. He expected the deportations to start on July 16.
"We are asking that they push back this date."

The change in the law has alarmed many of the estimated 200,000 Nicaraguans in Miami. Many fled the left-wing Sandinista government in the 1980s and were welcomed with open arms in the United States, that was arming anti-Sandinista rebels in Nicaragua at the time.
After the war ended in 1990, many Nicaraguans continued to emigrate because of economic hardship at home.
Alvarez said the U.S. ambassador to Nicaragua, Lino Gutierrez, had assured him there would not be a sudden, mass deportation.
Nicaragua is one of the poorest countries in Latin America, with 50 percent unemployment and a housing shortage.
